subject.title: Transcript redaction corrupts Anthropic/Bedrock reasoning signatures (AIza/LTAI false positive), causing persistent replay_invalid

question: For provider-minted signed-thinking fields, should OpenClaw preserve structurally valid opaque replay tokens even when their bytes contain credential-shaped substrings, or keep the current redaction-idempotency gate and only harden individual secret patterns?
rationale: The current tests deliberately redact credential-shaped provider signature fields, but the report shows that policy can corrupt real opaque replay tokens; maintainers need to choose the transcript redaction boundary before automation changes it.

options.title: Scoped Structural Preservation
options.body: Preserve valid opaque signatures only in known provider signed-thinking fields while still redacting arbitrary text, missing-route fields, malformed payloads, and sibling secrets.

options.title: Pattern-Only Hardening
options.body: Make fixed-case vendor prefixes and boundaries stricter while keeping the current idempotent-redaction requirement for provider signatures.

options.title: Send-Side Recovery Only
options.body: Drop visibly corrupted Bedrock/Anthropic thinking blocks during replay and repair, but leave transcript redaction behavior unchanged.

recommendation.title: Scoped Structural Preservation
recommendation.body: Preserve valid opaque signatures only in known provider signed-thinking fields while still redacting arbitrary text, missing-route fields, malformed payloads, and sibling secrets.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame points to this person across the active redaction, tests, and Bedrock replay surfaces touched by the decision.
